subject: Theory of Computation
notes: A DFA (Deterministic Finite Automaton) is a finite-state machine in which each state has exactly one transition for every input symbol. An NFA (Nondeterministic Finite Automaton) can have multiple transitions for the same input symbol or no transition at all. NFAs may also use epsilon transitions, which move between states without consuming input. Both DFAs and NFAs recognize exactly the class of regular languages. Every NFA can be converted into an equivalent DFA using the subset construction, although the DFA may have exponentially more states.
expected: Summary of DFA vs NFA; definitions of DFA, NFA, epsilon transition; mentions subset construction and regular languages; every question answerable from the notes; no facts beyond the notes.

subject: Operating Systems
notes: CPU scheduling decides which ready process runs next. First-Come First-Served (FCFS) runs processes in arrival order and is simple but can cause the convoy effect, where short processes wait behind a long one. Shortest Job First (SJF) picks the process with the smallest next CPU burst and gives the minimum average waiting time, but it needs to know burst lengths in advance and can starve long processes. Round Robin (RR) gives each process a fixed time quantum in turn; if the quantum is too large RR behaves like FCFS, and if it is too small context-switch overhead increases.
expected: Summary of FCFS, SJF, RR with trade-offs (convoy effect, starvation, quantum size); questions and answers match the notes only.

subject: DBMS
notes: Normalization reduces redundancy and update anomalies in relational schemas. A table is in First Normal Form (1NF) if all attributes hold atomic values and there are no repeating groups. A table is in Second Normal Form (2NF) if it is in 1NF and no non-key attribute depends on only part of a composite primary key. A table is in Third Normal Form (3NF) if it is in 2NF and no non-key attribute depends transitively on the primary key. Decomposition should be lossless so that the original table can be recovered by joining the parts.
expected: Definitions of 1NF, 2NF, 3NF as stated; mention of lossless decomposition; one correct option per MCQ.

subject: Computer Networks
notes: TCP is connection-oriented: it uses a three-way handshake to set up a connection, guarantees ordered and reliable delivery using acknowledgements and retransmissions, and provides flow control and congestion control. UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery, ordering or duplicate protection, but it has lower overhead and latency. TCP is used by applications such as web browsing and email, while UDP is used where speed matters more than reliability, such as live video streaming and DNS queries.
expected: TCP vs UDP comparison (handshake, reliability, overhead, use cases); no invented port numbers or header details.

subject: NLP
notes: An n-gram is a contiguous sequence of n tokens from a text. A unigram uses one token, a bigram uses two and a trigram uses three. An n-gram language model estimates the probability of a word given the previous n-1 words, for example P(w_i | w_{i-1}) for a bigram model. Counts from a training corpus are used to estimate these probabilities. Unseen n-grams get zero probability, so smoothing techniques such as add-one (Laplace) smoothing are used to give them a small non-zero probability.
expected: Definitions of n-gram, unigram/bigram/trigram, smoothing with add-one; questions use only these facts.

subject: Prompt Engineering
notes: Zero-shot prompting gives the model an instruction with no examples. Few-shot prompting adds a small number of input-output examples to the prompt so the model can imitate the pattern and format. Chain-of-thought prompting asks the model to reason step by step before giving the final answer, which often helps on multi-step problems. Prompt chaining splits a complex task into several smaller prompts where the output of one prompt becomes the input of the next. Output format constraints, such as asking for JSON, make responses easier to check and use in programs.
expected: Zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, chaining and format constraints defined as in the notes; no extra techniques.
